source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A town of smiths deep under the mountains and the mountain roads around it: forge fires glowing through the dark, hammers ringing on anvils, an old oath to the smith god, stubborn and proud people. Sturdy, proud and hard-working, a marching work song with weight and dignity, warm under its iron. Tempo 100 BPM, 4/4 time, key of D dorian. Instrumentation: low brass (tuba and horns), cellos and basses, hammered dulcimer, a bagpipe-like drone, anvil strikes on the beat, frame drums, a wordless low male hum (no words). Form: anvil and drum pickup; section A horn melody over the marching bass; section B dulcimer melody, warmer and a little wistful; a short interlude with only drone and anvils; section A again with full brass. Duration: 90 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
